chapters.title: Chapter 16: Landmark Cases—Nken v. Holder and the Law of Stays
chapters.reason: This chapter explicitly teaches the Nken framework. Including excerpts from the Nken opinion (the Court's articulation of the four-factor stay test and its discussion of the relative weighting of likelihood of success and irreparable harm) is necessary to present the authoritative language courts cite and to show how to apply the test in practice.

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Landmark Cases—Trump v. Hawaii, Mandel, and Deference in Entry Restrictions
chapters.reason: The chapter centers on Trump v. Hawaii's interpretation of 8 U.S.C. §1182(f) and the deferential standard for executive entry restrictions. Including key excerpts from the Trump majority opinion (and its reasoning on statutory scope and judicial deference) is essential for accurately conveying the controlling doctrinal text that students and practitioners will rely on.
